title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks
lede: United Airlines will block third-party AI agents from booking flights and managing reservations for customers, citing security risks and federal rules that require a human for some steps.

points: United warns that giving AI assistants account logins can leak data and trigger unintended purchases or MileagePlus spending.
Federal rules require a person to complete check-in, including confirming bags hold no banned items.
The restrictions apply on United's own platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators.
Booking, ticketing and distribution policies are being updated to enforce it.
Banks including Bank of America have warned customers against sharing passwords with AI assistants.

sections.text: Agents that work by reusing a customer's login are losing access at large companies, which makes shared credentials a fragile basis for any booking or shopping agent.
